Not by default. December 22nd falls inside the year-end code freeze (Dec 15 to Jan 5), when Finance runs the annual close. According to the project's release-process memory, no production release may go out in that window, hotfixes included, unless a lead in #fin-eng signs off in the channel first.

**To release on Dec 22nd:**
1. Get a lead in #fin-eng to sign off in the channel. Since Finance is asking for the fix, they're probably willing, but it still needs to be in writing there.
2. Complete the release checklist in the PR template, then tag from main as `vYYYY.MM.N` (for example `v2026.12.1`). CI builds and publishes, so don't publish by hand.
3. After staging promotes automatically, someone on the billing team has to approve the production deploy in the CI UI.

Dec 22nd is a Tuesday, so the Friday-after-14:00-UTC avoidance rule doesn't apply. If the sign-off doesn't come through, the fix would have to go out before Dec 15 or wait until after Jan 5.

I took the freeze dates from a stored memory and haven't checked them against a current source, so confirm them in #fin-eng when you ask for the sign-off. If the fix includes a database migration, it has to ship in the same release as the code that needs it.
